assistant_content:
The air at 18,000 feet didn’t just feel thin; it felt like a physical weight pressing against the inside of Elias’s skull. He paused, his crampons biting into the icy crust of the Khumbu Icefall, and looked back at the rope team trailing behind him. There were only two left: Sarah, his lead climber, and young Kael, who was struggling with the sheer verticality of the seracs.

"Keep your eyes up, Kael," Elias called out, his voice muffled by his balaclava. "Don’t look down. The ice doesn’t care
